- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect downward risk.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above prior peak.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative (or vice versa), model lags in adjusting; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to align with sentiment reversal.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values (neutral or bearish), model often fails to anticipate sharp drops; add 2–5% buffer below forecast for such periods.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (first 5–7 days), model often misses it; adjust downward by 2–5% in first 3–5 days of forecast.
